name: Rostral interstitial nucleus of the MLF (vertical gaze center)
summary: The vertical counterpart of the PPRF. The riMLF lies in the rostral midbrain tegmentum near the junction with the thalamus, just above the oculomotor nucleus, and its burst neurons generate vertical and torsional saccades. It receives cortical and collicular commands and projects to the oculomotor and trochlear nuclei of both sides, the up-gaze fibers crossing in the posterior commissure. Nearby, the interstitial nucleus of Cajal integrates vertical gaze holding. Lesions of the riMLF or the posterior commissure produce the vertical gaze palsies of the dorsal midbrain syndrome and of top-of-the-basilar strokes.

anatomy.location: Rostral midbrain tegmentum at the mesodiencephalic junction, dorsomedial to the red nucleus and rostral to the oculomotor nuclei, near the posterior commissure and the interstitial nucleus of Cajal.

function: Generates vertical (up and down) and torsional saccades and, with the interstitial nucleus of Cajal, holds vertical gaze position.

bestView.label: mesodiencephalic junction dorsomedial to the red nucleus
rostral midbrain tegmentum below the posterior commissure

imaging.normalAppearance: Not resolved; the lesions that cause vertical gaze palsy are paramedian rostral midbrain or bilateral thalamomesencephalic infarcts, best seen on DWI, or dorsal midbrain compression on sagittal T2.

pathology.finding: Bilateral paramedian thalamic and rostral midbrain restricted diffusion with vertical gaze palsy and somnolence.
Midbrain atrophy with the hummingbird sign on sagittal T1; vertical saccades slow long before the palsy is complete.
pathology.timing: Atrophy is visible by the time down-gaze is clearly impaired

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: DWI for infarcts; sagittal T1 for midbrain atrophy

lesionEffects.mechanism: riMLF burst neurons; a unilateral lesion mainly impairs down-gaze
Posterior commissure carrying crossed up-gaze fibers (Parinaud)
Vestibular pathways reach the nuclei directly: the palsy is supranuclear

examination: Vertical saccades and pursuit separately for up and down
Vertical oculocephalic reflex to show a supranuclear palsy
Look for lid retraction and convergence-retraction nystagmus
pearls: Down-gaze palsy points to the riMLF, up-gaze palsy to the posterior commissure
A supranuclear vertical gaze palsy (overcome by head movement) in a falling elderly patient suggests progressive supranuclear palsy
